item.title: Ex-captain Moody joins England in emotional haka response
item.description: Lewis Moody walked with current England captain Maro Itoje to join England's side to face New Zealand's haka [Getty Images] Former England captain Lewis Moody joined the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium. Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) last year, stood at the centre of England's line-up - between captain Maro Itoje and one of the team's vice-captains, Ellis Genge - as they faced up to the traditional pre-match challenge. Led by Genge's fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George, England then advanced to form a V shape, similar to the formation they took before last year's victory and the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final win against the All Blacks. Moody, who was embraced by most of England's team in the aftermath of the challenge and its acceptance, also delivered the match ball. Superb England run up record win over New Zealand England stars to help launch Moody MND challenge at All Blacks match With Twickenham energised, England started the match fast, with Henry Slade getting on the end of a Fin Smith grubber kick to score the first try after just four minutes. They went on to win 37-12, which was a record margin of victory for England over New Zealand. England coach Steve Borthwick told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It was particularly significant. What was really powerful was Lewis did the shirt presentations last night and he spoke unbelievably in the way he put his message across and it really resonated with the players. "It was some way to start a big game of rugby." All of England's players wore boots emblazoned with the logo of Moody's Front Up to MND campaign, to which signed warm-up and match-worn shirts will be donated. The campaign's first fundraising drive is a mass-participation coastal walk in June, which aims to raise more than £1m to fund research into the disease. A statement from England Rugby said: "As a hugely respected former England captain, it was important to the England men's team to show their support for Lewis and to involve him in many areas of the match day, including on the pitch. "Supporting Lewis and Front Up reflects the game's commitment to standing alongside those affected by MND, and to help raise awareness and funds for research." Moody delivered the match ball before England's victory over Australia last autumn, a few weeks after he revealed his diagnosis in an interview with BBC Breakfast. Last weekend, Wales players were bathed in red light and smoke during the All Blacks' haka in a response that was 'a year in the making'.

item.title: Matanović the difference maker as Freiburg extract victory in Elversberg
item.description: Matanović the difference maker as Freiburg extract victory in Elversberg Despite failing to muster up their best this afternoon, SC Freiburg secured a hard-fought 1-0 win over SV Elversberg. Igor Matanović pounced on one of very few chances for the visitors to leave the Saarland with three points. Scoring opportunities were few and far between in the Saarland as both teams fought for control. Francis Onyeka's mazy run caused some panic for Freiburg on 17 minutes that required an intervention from Philipp Lienhart. The first shot on target eventually fell the way of the hosts midway through the half. David Mokwa connected with a Lukas Petkov corner, however Mio Backhaus showed sharp reactions to divert it over his own crossbar. Freiburg's offensive output barely improved as the second-half rolled on. Julian Schuster's men only managed to register five shots before the hour mark, of which none managed to test Elversberg shot-stopper Nicolas Kristof. Wagner's side seemed more likely to score, threatening again on the hour. Felix Keidel picked off a Backhaus clearance and laid it off to Onyeka. The Leverkusen loanee's last involvement was blocked by Maxi Eggestein. Nonetheless, the Breisgau side snatched a precious 1-0 lead. Lienhart's long ball caught out Maximilian Rohr. Jan-Niklas Beste pounced, assisting Igor Matanović who picked out the lower-right corner with sheer precision. The hosts threw on Maurice Krattenmacher and Tom Zimmerscheid in desperation. When Yuito Suzuki steered home, the game result appeared final. However, an offside call bailed out Elversberg to give them fighting hope. Ultimately, said hope would be extinguished upon the final whistle as Freiburg held out. The win sees the Breisgau club pull level with second-place Bayern Munich, equal on points with only goal difference separating the two.

item.title: Nmecha helps Dortmund beat Gladbach to top Bundesliga
item.description: Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha celebrates after scoring on Saturday. (INA FASSBENDER) Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday. Bayern Munich's 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha's late strike. Dortmund are now outright first on 24 points, with Bayern and Freiburg, who won 1-0 at Elversberg, locked on 22 points. Bayern also lost Harry Kane to injury in Friday's draw, with the Ballon d'Or winner set to miss several months after undergoing surgery on his injured ankle earlier on Saturday. Dortmund, who travel to Arsenal on Tuesday, knew victory would send them top but the 2024 Champions League finalists had few chances against a stubborn Gladbach. Nmecha, who scored twice in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elversberg before the international break, looked most likely when his header forced a save from Daniel Batz. With 17 minutes left, Marcel Sabitzer chipped a free-kick inches wide of the post. Dortmund continued to push and Nmecha was on hand to knock a rebound through Batz's fingers and help the visitors snare a crucial three points. Igor Matanovic's 68th-minute strike helped Freiburg break down promoted Elversberg and move level with Bayern. Last season's Europa League finalists Freiburg stay one point ahead of fourth-placed RB Leipzig, who romped to a 5-1 victory at Union Berlin. Antonio Nusa, Romulo, Brajan Gruda, Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku scored for Leipzig, who host Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday. Gruda was particularly impressive with a goal and an assist, just days after impressing for Jurgen Klopp's Germany with a goal and two assists versus the Netherlands on the other side of the German capital. Elsewhere, Afonso Moreira broke his Bundesliga duck with a brace in Bayer Leverkusen's 4-0 home win over Paderborn. Moreira had failed to find the net since his summer move from Lyon but scored Leverkusen's first two goals and laid on one for Ezequiel Fernandez. Patrik Schick also got a goal to move level with Niclas Fuellkrug atop the league goalscoring charts with nine goals. Jonathan Burkardt scored the only goal as Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hoffenheim at home. Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved a first-half Andrej Kramaric penalty to keep his remarkable spot-kick record alive. Atubolu has saved seven out of the 11 penalties he has faced, which is the best save percentage in the Bundesliga's 64-year history. item.title: Fernandez dropped, Anderson scores - Man City's £327m midfield dilemma
item.description: Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi both joined Manchester City in the summer [Getty Images] There may have been some eyebrows raised before kick-off when Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca decided to drop club record signing Enzo Fernandez to the bench against Fulham. Fernandez's lengthy excursions back home to Argentina for their two fixtures during the international break may have been a factor in Maresca's thinking when selecting his starting XI for this game. If it was, the Italian refrained from giving that as a reason. "I just think for this game it's better having Ayyoub Bouaddi in there," he told TNT Sports shortly before kick-off. Even so, the move was a significant one as his side were in desperate need of victory after suffering three straight Premier League defeats. That winless streak extended to four after being held to a 1-1 draw. Maresca had an opportunity to fix the issues in his set-up during the two-week break and admitted on Friday he was searching for "more balance" in the "defensive line, midfield and up front". The pairing of the steady Bouaddi and all-action Elliot Anderson in the centre of the park was the crucial call, and it may have given Maresca some idea as to how to approach the forthcoming run of games. "Ayyoub with Elliot were both really good," said Maresca. "Today we used Elliot a bit more attacking midfielder, he arrived inside the box and scored a fantastic goal, he had three or four moments around the box where he was really dangerous. "It is another solution for us. In this moment, we are trying to know each other more as players and also to find the right solution." item.description: Burkardt secures hard-fought Frankfurt victory against Hoffenheim On a seven-degree Saturday afternoon at Deutsche Bank Park, two mid-table sides went head-to-head in the tenth matchweek of the 2026/27 Bundesliga season as Eintracht Frankfurt (3-3-3, 10th) played host to TSG 1899 Hoffenheim (4-0-5, 9th). Frankfurt, coached by Adi Hütter, have won three of their last five matches in all competitions - unbeaten in their last three, with two wins against Hamburger SV in both Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal (3-1, 3-1) and a draw with SC Paderborn 07 (2-2). Of the eight goals that Frankfurt registered in those matches, six were in the second half. On the other side of the field is Hoffenheim - also led by an Austrian coach, Christian Ilzer - who have had a tight schedule split between the Bundesliga and UEFA Europa League, but managed to pick up points in four out of their last five matches. In the Bundesliga itself, Die Kraichgauer have managed six points out of a potential twelve through their last four matches, defeating Borussia Mönchengladbach (2-1) and FC Schalke 04 (2-1). In terms of head-to-head record between the two sides, Frankfurt went into this match 3-1-1 through the last five encounters. In all five matches, four goals were scored between the two sides. All three Frankfurt victories, including the away win in last season’s campaign, were by 3-1 results; the lone defeat, at home in 2025/26, was also by a 3-1 score. The draw finished 2-2. item.title: Unbeaten Lazio maintain Serie A lead, Como fourth
item.description: Tijjani Noslin (L) celebrates scoring Lazio's second goal against Lecce (Alberto PIZZOLI) Lazio will continue their surprise stay at the top of Serie A for at least another week after thumping Lecce 3-0 on Saturday to move four points clear at the summit. Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio extended their lead over Inter Milan -- at struggling Atalanta on Sunday night -- thanks to goals in each half from Tijjani Noslin and a late Davide Frattesi strike. It was a straightforward win in Rome over a Lecce team now winless in five matches, with just one point collected in that run. Lazio looked to be in turmoil heading into this season, with a long-standing fan protest against owner Claudio Lotito leaving the Stadio Olimpico sparsely populated for home matches. But they have dropped just four points since the start of the season and are yet to be beaten after 12 matches. Como stay six points behind the leaders in fourth with a 2-0 home win over Cagliari. Cesc Fabregas' team welcome AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday before hosting Juventus next weekend. AC Milan will move back into the top four ahead of Como with a home win over high-flying Frosinone on Sunday. Lazio's local rivals Roma, five points back in third, take on Parma on Saturday evening ahead of a daunting trip to European champions Paris Saint-Germain. item.title: Man City boss Maresca fumes over Haaland controversy in Fulham draw
item.description: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland had a crucial goal disallowed against Fulham (Oli SCARFF) Enzo Maresca insisted it was "quite clear" that Erling Haaland was wrongly denied a crucial goal in Manchester City's damaging 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday. Maresca's side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz's early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland's equaliser was contentiously ruled out. The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line. But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision. Referee Thomas Bramall ruled that Leno had not lost control because the ball was between his hands and VAR Sam Barrott upheld the call. "I reviewed the goal after the game. From my point of view, it's quite clear that it's not a foul, but I'm not the guy that decides, unfortunately," Maresca said. Asked how Haaland viewed the incident, Maresca said: "When they were reviewing the VAR, he was absolutely sure that it was a goal, because I asked him from the touchline. "He was completely sure that it was a goal but the referee decided for different things." Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season. But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time. Despite the fans' frustration, Maresca tried to accentuate the positives. Anderson's second goal for City in all competitions was a welcome boost after his red card in England's Nations League win against Spain in midweek. "It was a nice moment for him, a nice moment for us because it gave us the chance to come back in the game," Maresca said. "We used him today for the first time as an attacking midfielder. He was playing a little bit more deep with us. "We are trying to find different solutions, the right balance, and to be more consistent." After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches. It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham. Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday. Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks. "For sure we don't like this kind of moments, in terms of four games in a row without a win," Maresca said. "But we also know that, unfortunately, it's normal or it's part of your path that you go through these kind of moments. "It's important that we find a way to keep a clean-sheet. Sometimes you need to win games 1-0." smg/ea

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached its last weekend of pool play with the finals weekend fate of the world’s top teams becoming clear. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. South Africa and New Zealand are assured of a top-two finish in their group – but both were beaten in a stunning penultimate round of pool action. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team.
